Record_source: Wearing feedback records; assistive-device configuration records
Case_context_and_user_feedback: The user reported posterior-knee discomfort and felt that the strap had to be tightened increasingly.
Current_EBOM_status: Insufficient space in the posterior contact area; strap tension was being used to compensate for inadequate fit; no local cushioning.
Confirmed_EBOM_difference: Posterior-knee clearance increased from approximately 2.7 mm to 3.6 mm; posterior-thigh strap pretension reduced from approximately 23 N to 20 N; a 2-mm posterior cushion was added; strap routing remained unchanged.
Adjustment_rationale_and_constraints: The source of posterior compression should be relieved rather than compensated for by further tightening the strap.
Reference_rule_name: Localized release for posterior-knee flexion compression

Record_source: Wearing feedback records; assistive-device configuration records
Case_context_and_user_feedback: During the early postoperative stage, the assistive device gradually slipped downward after 15 minutes of continuous walking, requiring the user to pull it upward manually.
Current_EBOM_status: The lower-leg section used a conventional straight circumferential strap; no anti-slip lining was provided; lower-leg pretension was approximately 16 N.
Confirmed_EBOM_difference: The main lower-leg strap path was changed from a straight circumferential route to a diagonal cross-over route; one silicone anti-slip lining was added to the medial lower-leg section, with a length of 80 mm and a width of 22 mm; lower-leg pretension was adjusted from approximately 16 N to 20–21 N; the thigh fixation points remained unchanged.
Adjustment_rationale_and_constraints: The slippage was mainly caused by insufficient retention in the lower-leg section, but the entire system must not be tightened in a way that creates new local compression.

Record_source: Electronic medical records; wearing feedback records; assistive-device configuration records
Case_context_and_user_feedback: During the early postoperative stage, the user reported that the posterior knee was pressed during knee flexion and sitting up, with greater pain at larger flexion angles.
Current_EBOM_status: The posterior-knee contact area used a conventional EVA pad; pad thickness was 4 mm; posterior-knee clearance was approximately 2.6 mm; the posterior boundary had no relief treatment.
Confirmed_EBOM_difference: The EVA pad in the posterior-knee contact area was reduced from 4 mm to 2.5 mm; posterior-knee clearance was adjusted from approximately 2.6 mm to 3.8 mm; a 3-mm rounded transition was added to the inner edge of the posterior pad; the main shell support structure remained unchanged.
Adjustment_rationale_and_constraints: The peak posterior pressure during flexion should be reduced without weakening the stable support required during the early postoperative stage.
Reference_rule_name: Localized release for posterior-knee flexion compression

Record_source: Electronic medical records; rehabilitation assessment records; assistive-device configuration records
Case_context_and_user_feedback: During the early postoperative stage, the physician required restricted knee range of motion, while the user reported insufficient support during knee flexion.
Current_EBOM_status: The hinge ROM limit was set to 90°; the support rods were standard straight rods; the medial and lateral support-rod connection points had not been reinforced.
Confirmed_EBOM_difference: The ROM limit was maintained at 90° rather than being increased; the medial and lateral support-rod screws were changed from M3 to M4; two end-stop pads were added to the support rods; the hinge-axis position remained unchanged.
Adjustment_rationale_and_constraints: Stable support should be prioritized during the protection stage, and the range of motion should not be released prematurely.
Reference_rule_name: Staged ROM control during the protection period

Record_source: Electronic medical records; wearing feedback records
Case_context_and_user_feedback: The user had substantial postoperative swelling and reported strong circumferential pressure from the shell, while the physician required protective support to be maintained.
Current_EBOM_status: The shell cavity had been designed for a non-swollen limb; the medial clearance was approximately 0.8 mm; the lateral clearance was approximately 1.0 mm; no adjustment allowance was provided for the swelling stage.
Confirmed_EBOM_difference: The key high-pressure regions of the shell cavity were expanded by 2–3 mm; one set of replaceable 2-mm cushioning pads was added; the lateral shell support ribs and hinge-connection positions remained unchanged.
Adjustment_rationale_and_constraints: Adjustment allowance should be preserved during the swelling stage without weakening the shell support frame required during the early postoperative stage.
